s2c_canonical_regression.finding: S2c structural selection over-selects identity records (+116) from OTHER tasks, displacing value records (-142) needed for the current task. Net effect on EXACT tasks: 8 improved, 8 regressed (CES flat at 0.350). Net effect on RESOLVED tasks: 20 improved, 2 regressed (CES 0.200→0.500). Overall CES: 0.192 (C4_0) → 0.425 (C4_4) vs 0.783 (C4_5 oracle).
s2c_canonical_regression.potential_fix: Make S2c's structural criterion task-aware: only prefer identity/link records that mention the current subject. This is a mechanism change requiring its own qualification.
s2c_canonical_regression.root_cause: S2c's structural criterion treats all identity/link records as equally valuable, but only identity/link records connected to the current subject are useful. Identity records from other tasks are distractors that displace answer-bearing value records.

exact_identity_over_expansion.critically_developable_without_qualifica: The asymmetry is present in DEVELOPMENT data at essentially the same magnitude (EXACT 31.6% vs RESOLVED 91.9% keep-rate). The selector fix can therefore be designed, implemented and certified entirely on development data, and confirmed later on a fresh untouched split -- there is no need, and no license, to tune against these qualification receipts.
exact_identity_over_expansion.finding: The selector's failure is concentrated almost entirely on tasks whose identity was already EXACT. Keep-rate of AVAILABLE required evidence, qualification: EXACT 27/122 = 22.1%, RESOLVED 90/98 = 91.8%. Development shows the same asymmetry: EXACT 18/57 = 31.6%, RESOLVED 34/37 = 91.9%.
exact_identity_over_expansion.hypothesis_this_motivates: Structural expansion is over-aggressive when the subject needs no resolution: with EXACT identity and a high-ranked candidate directly expressing the target relation, the answer-bearing record should be preserved before structural expansion fills the remaining budget. For RESOLVED/abbreviation cases the broader S2c behavior is clearly helping (+0.2250) and should be kept. That is an information-state-routed selector, not a global policy change.
exact_identity_over_expansion.strongest_form: 32 of the 95 EXACT-identity drops on qualification dropped evidence the retriever had ranked FIRST in fusion. Retrieval had already solved those tasks and the selector discarded the answer.

qualification_failure_decomposition.headline_finding_bottleneck_inversion: The dominant bottleneck INVERTED between splits. On development the selector was the largest lane (35.0% vs retrieval 21.7%); on qualification retrieval dominates (55.6% vs selector 21.0%). Development work would therefore naturally have chased the selector, because that is where the visible headroom was, while the thing that actually broke generalization was retrieval -- which looked healthy on development (candidate CES 0.7833) and roughly halved on qualification (0.4440). This is the single most useful output of the qualification run: it says the next sprint's priority is NOT what development's own numbers would have suggested.

identity_is_not_the_constraint.note: 99% EXACT or RESOLVED, so S2c was active on 495/500. The I3 mechanism from Gate C3 is doing its job; 'identity failed on qualification' is ruled out as an explanation. The 5 AMBIGUOUS cases are the designed abstain path.

qualification_failure_decomposition.method: Every task lands in exactly one bucket of a mutually exclusive, exhaustive chain following the pipeline's own stages: A_RETRIEVAL (required evidence never reached the candidate pool), B_SELECTOR (it was in the pool and the selector dropped it), C_READER (it survived into the packet and HRM still answered wrong), SUCCESS. Verified exhaustive/exclusive by test, including the case where a wrong-evidence task happens to answer correctly (still counted against retrieval, so A cannot be understated).

reader_is_not_the_constraint.note: Given correct evidence the reader generalizes nearly unchanged from 120 to 500 held-out tasks, and only 10.0% of qualification tasks fail with complete evidence in the packet. Do not spend effort on HRM recurrence or reader capacity; the memory system around it is the constraint.

selector_efficiency_did_not_collapse.note: S2c's efficiency at preserving AVAILABLE complete sets is nearly unchanged (55.3% -> 52.7%). Most of its absolute degradation is inherited from a much worse input pool, not from the selector getting worse. This is what separates 'retrieval regressed' from 'selector regressed'.

two_independent_research_lanes.conclusion: These are two independent problems with different owners and different experiments, not one 'C4 fix'. Retrieval is the larger lane by task count (55.6% vs 21.0%) and can be worked without HRM at all (retrieval-only CES@k / required-evidence recall on frozen pools). The selector lane is smaller but has the cleaner, better-localized hypothesis.

retrieval_dominated_families.note: temporal_chain has the full evidence set in the candidate pool for only 6% of tasks. No selector can fix that; it is a retrieval/representation problem and the sharpest available diagnostic for the retrieval lane.

selector_dominated_families.note: entity_attribute has near-perfect availability (0.98) and the selector still keeps the needed evidence only 52% of the time. Pure selector headroom, no retrieval work required to exploit it.

comparison_to_development.interpretation: The mechanism's development-measured gain (+0.20) roughly halved on held-out data (+0.091), missing the pre-registered D4 threshold (+0.15). This looks like a genuine generalization gap concentrated in retrieval/selection quality (C4_5 dropped much more than C4_6, the reader-only ceiling), not a collapse of the reader or a catastrophic single-family failure (D5 passed).

no_mechanism_baseline_c4_0.note: also drops -- qualification's task distribution is harder overall, not just harder for the mechanism specifically

oracle_selection_c4_5.note: large drop -- oracle selection over the real (non-oracle) candidate pool degrades substantially on qualification's task distribution, well beyond what the reader-ceiling comparison alone would suggest

reader_ceiling_c4_6.note: nearly unchanged -- the HRM reader's raw capability given oracle evidence generalizes fine

verified_diagnostic_qualification_split._note: Independently recomputed from the frozen receipts. Qualification-split only, so unaffected by the v3 OOD defects. This is the cleanest available proof that the failure is retrieval infrastructure and not the reader.

verified_diagnostic_qualification_split.reader_error_is_not_uniform: The 0.172 reader error concentrates in boolean (0.650) and enum (0.698) judgments, not numeric/symbolic extraction. Inspect those before any evidence-use training.

gate_c1_v4_ladder.claim: On frozen controlled_gate_a_v4 with the mechanism pinned at 3260ce0, the current retrieval path is near-inert: R1 two-pass reaches 0.062 qualification / 0.016 OOD against an oracle-evidence ceiling of 0.880 / 0.908.
gate_c1_v4_ladder.critical_reading_of_R3_to_R4: R4's complete-set success is only 0.168 while its quality is 0.462, so R4 answers many tasks from PARTIAL gold evidence. The +0.408 gain is therefore not 'better ranking' -- it is the effect of removing every non-gold record. Any distractor in the packet is close to catastrophic, and the reader can often work from an incomplete but clean packet. Do not read R3->R4 as a pure selection-ranking term.
not_a_claim_about: any receipt-verified figure: the run's receipts were not pushed to this repository
selection ranking, since R4's gain comes from removing all non-gold records, not from ranking

gate_c1_v4_ladder.provenance: Measured on Colab T4 at pinned commit 3b1fbd5, sequential generation (batch_equivalence_passed=false, batch_size=1). Values transcribed from the run output; the receipt files were not pushed back to this repository, so they are NOT independently re-verifiable here.

gate_c2_bge_dense.claim: A stronger pinned dense encoder (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, CLS pooling, query-prefix only) earns promotion on OOD but not on qualification. Complete-set@50 rises 0.072 -> 0.152 OOD (more than doubling) while qualification moves only 0.364 -> 0.370.
gate_c2_bge_dense.claim_class_note: The numbers stand (BGE OOD CES@50 0.152 vs MiniLM 0.072; description 0.083 -> 0.242). But this OOD set has now been used to decide whether BGE belongs in the architecture, so it is no longer a pristine final confirmation set for THIS C2 architecture-selection question. Class changed from 'final untouched confirmation' to 'measured exploratory evidence used for architecture selection'. A clean confirmation requires controlled_gate_c2_calibration_v1.
gate_c2_bge_dense.description_component_caveat: The +0.14/+0.159 description gains were measured on the ambiguous corpus. They may show that BGE retrieves semantically related text better, but they do NOT establish entity-level description handling and must not be cited as such until reproduced on an identifiable corpus.
gate_c2_bge_dense.interpretation: The entire OOD gain comes from the DESCRIPTION regime (+0.158, roughly 3x). That is mechanistically coherent: a description is a natural-language phrase, which is what a semantic encoder is for. An alias is an arbitrary name substitution that no encoder can resolve without retrieving the identity record, so alias remains a multi-hop retrieval problem rather than an embedding problem. Promoting BGE on aggregate recall alone would have obscured that split.
not_a_claim_about: qualification, where the gain is +0.006 and within noise
alias resolution, which improves only +0.008 and is not a semantic-similarity problem
downstream answer quality, which was not measured here
gate_c2_bge_dense.promotion_wording: bge-small-en-v1.5 is promoted as the preferred dense representation for semantic-description OOD retrieval in V4 and as a candidate dense arm for Gate C2 fusion. NOT 'the best retriever'.

gate_c2_description_diagnostic.claim: Staged funnel over all 150 description tasks. Identity retrieval, mention recognition, and resolver response are all 1.000; canonical correctness is 0.00-0.12. ResolutionRate 1.000 with ResolutionPrecision 0.00-0.12, dominant class AMBIGUOUS_MATCH. Root cause: only 4 descriptor phrases exist per corpus, so one description string refers to up to 13 different entities and the question does not identify a unique referent.
gate_c2_description_diagnostic.consequence: The v3 description verdict measured an ill-posed regime, not a mechanism limitation. The oracle arm reached 1.000 only by reading true canonical identity from _oracle_metadata, bypassing an ambiguity no runtime resolver can resolve. All description-regime figures in C2-C-v1/v2/v3 and the description component of the BGE policy comparison are VOIDED as mechanism measurements. Canonical, abbreviation, and alias are unaffected.
not_a_claim_about: the resolver's capability on well-posed references
canonical, abbreviation, or alias regimes, which are unaffected
any promotion decision
gate_c2_description_diagnostic.why_prior_protocols_missed_it: Absolute deltas made a near-zero gain look like a near-miss (+0.08 vs +0.10). Oracle-gap normalisation exposed the magnitude; only separating resolution RATE from resolution PRECISION found the cause. The resolver was always answering, and always wrong.

gate_c2_dev_sweep.CRITICAL_CONFOUND: The development split contains ONLY the canonical and abbreviation regimes -- it has no description regime at all, because description and alias are held out for OOD. BGE's entire measured value was the description regime (0.083 -> 0.242 OOD). Development therefore CANNOT select for the capability BGE provides, and freezing the retriever on development alone would discard it for the wrong reason. The retriever freeze must not be decided on development complete-set alone.
gate_c2_dev_sweep.claim: Development-only sweep. Q3 formulation matters enormously: keeping the SUBJECT in the query alongside bridge and relation lifts complete-set@50 from 0.625 (bridge+relation) to 0.900 (subject+bridge+relation). RRF k is flat across {10,30,60,100} at 0.767. On development BM25 dominates both dense arms and contributes 25 unique gold records against 2 each for MiniLM and BGE.
not_a_claim_about: qualification or OOD, which were not touched
Q3 as a production mechanism -- it is oracle-informed
downstream HRM quality

gate_c2_policy_arms.alias_decomposition_overturns_the_prior_: I predicted in advance that alias would fail because no arm traverses an identity record. The decomposition says otherwise: identity_record_recall is 0.96-1.00 on the surface partition, so identity records ARE being retrieved. The shortfall is target_recall_given_identity_found at 0.61-0.80, and complete-set at only 0.21-0.26. The bottleneck is assembling the COMPLETE multi-record proof path after identity is in hand, not finding the identity record. This reframes C2-I from 'identity resolution' toward chain completion.
gate_c2_policy_arms.claim: On frozen calibration, judged against rules predeclared before the run: P1_bge passes description (+0.14) but destroys canonical (-0.30). P2_rrf_bm25_bge holds canonical (-0.02, exactly at threshold) and abbreviation (+0.04) but misses the description bar at +0.08 against a required +0.10. Neither is promotable.
not_a_claim_about: the holdout partition, which was not evaluated
downstream HRM quality, not measured here
any threshold revision; the bar was frozen and is not being moved
gate_c2_policy_arms.replication: BGE's description advantage REPLICATES on a fresh corpus with fully disjoint vocabulary (+0.14 alone, +0.08 in fusion), so it is a real property of the regime rather than a V4 artifact. That is the strongest positive result here, even though the arm fails.
gate_c2_policy_arms.verdict: FAIL_CANDIDATE_COVERAGE for both P1_bge and P2_rrf_bm25_bge

gate_c2_protocol.claim: Gate C2 promotion rules, reference arm, and selection threshold are predeclared in configs/gate_c2_protocol.json before any calibration measurement. Reference arm is P0_bm25 and marked immutable; primary metric is complete_set@50; per-regime rules are canonical >= -0.02, abbreviation >= -0.02, description >= +0.10, alias report-only; tau_selection = 0.05 for the S0/S5 gate.

gate_c2_query_ladder.claim: Q0-Q3 retrieval-only query ablation on frozen V4. Querying the bridge entity ALONE (Q1) is worse than the original question on both splits and collapses to 0.000 complete-set@50 on OOD, which explains why the V4 ladder's R2 did not beat R1. A fully rendered request (Q3) nearly doubles dense complete-set@10 on qualification (0.214 -> 0.416) and lifts fusion complete-set@50 from 0.426 to 0.614. On OOD even a perfect query reaches only 0.200, so retrieval representation, not query formulation, is the binding constraint there.
gate_c2_query_ladder.implication: Query formulation is a real opportunity on qualification but is NOT sufficient on OOD. Building a semantic gap reasoner alone would sit on top of an index that cannot exploit a perfect query out of distribution. Retrieval representation must improve alongside it.
not_a_claim_about: downstream answer quality, which was not measured in this ablation
any learned query formulator, since Q1-Q3 are oracle-constructed
selection, which is measured separately on frozen candidate pools

gate_c2c_chain_completion.claim: Bounded runtime chain completion produces large gains on the primary metric but fails a secondary conditional criterion that I specified badly. All four runtime arms clear five of six predeclared checks and fail only target_recall_given_identity_delta.
gate_c2c_chain_completion.mechanism_finding: Chain completion is highly effective. On c2_cal_id complete-set rises 0.710 -> 0.980, essentially reaching the 1.000 oracle-evidence ceiling. On c2_cal_surface it rises 0.260 -> 0.560. Alias improves +0.42 and abbreviation +0.52 against a required +0.10, with zero canonical regression and depth within the bound of 2. Canonicalization is purely runtime: identity statements are parsed out of retrieved candidate text, never read from _oracle_metadata.
gate_c2c_chain_completion.my_specification_error: Choosing a near-saturated conditional metric as a REQUIRED promotion criterion was a protocol-design mistake, made by me before the run. The correct response is not to move the bar after seeing results -- that would destroy the value of predeclaring. The verdict stands as FAIL. A successor protocol must predeclare criteria with measurable headroom, and these numbers are then exploratory with respect to that successor.
not_a_claim_about: promotion; the frozen bar was not met and is not being moved
the holdout partition, untouched
downstream HRM quality, not measured
gate_c2c_chain_completion.semantics_note: experiment_verdict FAIL means the predeclared promotion criterion was not met. It does NOT mean the mechanism had no effect; mechanism_effect_observed is true and large. Historical verdicts are unchanged; the status model is now expressive enough to hold both facts at once.
gate_c2c_chain_completion.verdict: FAIL_CHAIN_COMPLETION under the frozen protocol, on one criterion only
gate_c2c_chain_completion.why_it_fails: target_recall_given_identity_delta required >= +0.05. Measured: C1 +0.0144, C2 -0.0857, C3 -0.0143, C4 +0.0469. The reference already scored 0.96 on c2_cal_id and 0.80 on c2_cal_surface for that metric, so at most 0.20 of headroom existed and I still required +0.05 of it as a hard gate. C4 misses by 0.0031.

gate_c2c_v2_chain_validation.replication_evidence: The chain-completion effect is now measured on THREE independent corpora with disjoint vocabularies. v1 surface 0.260 -> 0.560, v2 surface 0.260 -> 0.570; v1 ID 0.710 -> 0.970, v2 ID 0.720 -> 0.980. Near-identical magnitudes across corpora that share no surface forms. This is a real mechanism, not benchmark exploitation.

gate_c2c_v2_chain_validation.the_reformulated_criterion_worked: v1's ill-posed absolute +0.05 on a near-saturated diagnostic is replaced by headroom closure, and it PASSED at 0.192. The reformulation was correct and is now validated on data it was not fitted to.
gate_c2c_v2_chain_validation.verdict: FAIL_CHAIN_COMPLETION on one endpoint; five of six pass
gate_c2c_v2_chain_validation.what_failed_and_why_it_is_not_the_mechan: description +0.08 vs required +0.10. Chain completion helps description least because a description question already resolves through one identity record; it has the shortest residual chain, so there is least for a follow-up to recover. The +0.10 bar was carried over from the policy-arm protocol where it measured a DIFFERENT intervention (a stronger encoder). Reusing an encoder-calibrated threshold for a chain-completion endpoint is a second protocol-specification error, distinct from v1's.

gate_c2c_v3_chain_validation.amended: The description FAIL measured an ambiguous-by-construction regime. See data/hrm/DESCRIPTION_REGIME_ERRATUM.md. The FAIL verdict is preserved unchanged; the description figure is voided as a mechanism measurement. Abbreviation (0.960) and alias (0.815) oracle-gap closure stand.
gate_c2c_v3_chain_validation.claim: Fourth disjoint corpus (river vocabulary), fixed C4, oracle-gap-closure protocol with uniform tau=0.25. Three of four regimes pass decisively: abbreviation OGC=0.960, alias OGC=0.815, canonical saturated-and-held. Description fails at OGC=0.025 against an oracle gap of 0.800 -- the largest headroom of any regime and almost none of it recovered.
not_a_claim_about: promotion; the bar was not met and is not moving
the reserved holdout, still untouched
downstream HRM quality
gate_c2c_v3_chain_validation.the_normalizer_worked: Oracle-gap closure was the right endpoint and it changed the diagnosis rather than merely the arithmetic. Under v2's absolute deltas, description looked like a near-miss (+0.08 vs +0.10). Normalized, it is a near-total failure: 0.025 of an available 0.800. The two prior protocols were hiding the single regime where the mechanism genuinely does not work.
gate_c2c_v3_chain_validation.what_this_isolates: Chain completion is real and large for abbreviation and alias -- where a retrieved identity record names a canonical entity that runtime parsing can extract. Description references resolve through prose ('the ancillary unit charted during survey season'), and the canonicalization parser recovers them far less reliably, so the follow-up query is built from a subject it never resolved. C5 reaching 1.000 proves the evidence is retrievable given the right query, so this is a canonicalization-coverage failure, not a retrieval-ceiling failure.

gate_c2s_relation_keyword_control.claim: The arm labelled S2_connectivity computes exactly as implemented but does not instantiate the chain-selection hypothesis it was built for. Its dominant term rewards records containing the target relation string. In this corpus 0/56 bridge records contain the target relation while 99/99 answer records do, so the arm cannot retain a bridge record: BridgeRetention=0.000 is arithmetically forced, not incidental. It fills 91.3% of each packet with relation-string matches, of which 79.3% of the packet are relation-matching records that are not required.
gate_c2s_relation_keyword_control.distinguished_from: the ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 arm, which was COMPUTATIONALLY invalid (NaN scores). This arm computes correctly; only its scientific interpretation was wrong. Its receipts are valid and retained.
gate_c2s_relation_keyword_control.historical_arm_id: S2_connectivity (unchanged in frozen receipts; renaming a measured arm id would break reproducibility)
gate_c2s_relation_keyword_control.kept_as: negative control: target-relation keyword matching is insufficient for multi-hop packing and causes systematic distractor selection
not_a_claim_about: whether relational chain selection works, which it does not test
the target relation being illegitimate input; it appears verbatim in 200/200 questions
the structural arms S2a/S2b/S2c, measured separately
final answer quality, where it was indistinguishable from S0
the reserved c2_cal_holdout, untouched
gate_c2s_relation_keyword_control.retained_because: On descv4_surface it is the only arm with a significant gain (+0.170, CI excluding zero under all three groupings, SGC 30.9%). Relation scoring needs no entity anchor, so it still works where identity resolution fails. It is a useful fallback baseline for weak-identity conditions, not a bad implementation to forget.

gate_c2s_selection_opportunity.claim: On frozen candidate pools with an identical 6-record packet budget, oracle selection beats raw top-N by +0.39 (descv4_id) and +0.55 (descv4_surface) HRM verified quality, against a predeclared tau of 0.05. Selection has a large real opportunity; S1-S4 are authorized.
not_a_claim_about: any runtime selector, none of which has been built or measured
the reserved holdout, still untouched
candidate discovery, which is frozen and held constant here
gate_c2s_selection_opportunity.why_conditional_metrics_matter: Retrieval is not being blamed for selection. Complete evidence is AVAILABLE in the pool for 0.95 and 0.74 of tasks, yet raw top-N retains it for only 0.46 and 0.22 of those available cases. The gap is selection discarding evidence the retriever already found.

gate_c2s_selector_arm_defect.claim: The first S3 cross-encoder arm was dead and silently reported the baseline. cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 returns NaN from its first attention layer onward for every query/document pair under torch 2.10 / transformers 5.14.1, with finite fp32 weights (absmax 4.7) and clean embeddings. Python compares NaN sort keys as all-False, so the pool came back unreordered and the arm produced metrics identical to S0 to four decimals.

diagnosis_evidence.model_specific: ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2 scores +7.52 relevant / -11.14 irrelevant and TinyBERT-L-2-v2 scores +6.92 / -11.42 on the same stack, so the defect is the L6 checkpoint, not the environment or the harness
diagnosis_evidence.nan_scores: 50/50 candidates non-finite on every task checked

gate_c2s_selector_arm_defect.fix: Added DegenerateRerankerError: a reranker returning any non-finite score, or one score for every candidate, now raises instead of emitting an order that duplicates the raw pool. Runs also record differs_from_s0 per arm, so a no-op arm is visible in the receipt. S3 is repinned to ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2 at a fixed revision.
not_a_claim_about: whether cross-encoder reranking helps selection, which remains unmeasured
any selector's effectiveness; no arm figures are claimed here
the descv4 partitions' selector results, still being measured
the reserved c2_cal_holdout, untouched
torch or transformers generally; only the L6 checkpoint is implicated
gate_c2s_selector_arm_defect.voided: The earlier partial descv4_id figures are void: they came from an uncommitted /tmp script that wrote no manifest before timing out, and they included the dead S3 arm. They are not carried forward as evidence.
gate_c2s_selector_arm_defect.why_it_mattered: Read naively, that arm said 'cross-encoder reranking does not help', which would have been a false negative about a component the roadmap depends on. The arm had not reranked anything.

gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.ablation: relation-only retains answers but destroys bridges (BridgeRetention 0.000); structure-only (S2b) retains bridges but collapses answer retention to 0.394 and LOSES quality (dQ=-0.100); structure plus relation as one component is the only combination that improves both and the only one that moves quality.

ceilings.note: S5 is the ceiling for SELECTION over the frozen candidate pool. It is not the pipeline ceiling and must not be conflated with R5-style oracle-evidence arms, which bypass more of the pipeline.

gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.claim: At packet budget 6 over the frozen pools, oracle selection is worth +0.390 quality on descv4_id (0.360 -> 0.750) and +0.550 on descv4_surface (0.130 -> 0.680), so evidence selection is a real and large lever. Of the runtime arms, only S2c_chain_plus_relation separates from S0 on descv4_id: dQ=+0.1200 with a paired grouped-bootstrap CI excluding zero under ALL THREE groupings (family [0.04,0.21], source_cluster [0.030,0.214], template [0.010,0.228]), capturing 30.8% of the oracle opportunity. S1/S2/S3/S4 and S2a/S2b do not separate from S0 on that partition.
gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.dual_mechanism_note: S2c appears to help through two distinct routes -- structural role recovery and packet cleanliness / distractor reduction -- which the current single score conflates. A future structural selector should make those terms explicit rather than fusing them.
gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.earned_claim: S2c improves evidence selection when the question entity can be resolved.
gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.mechanism_evidence: Correct->wrong flips attribute pointwise failures to role loss: S1 loses the identity record on 10 of 13, S3 the answer record on 10 of 16, S4 answer on 8 and identity on 4 of 13. S2c's 22 fixes break down as 14 answer newly retained, 8 bridge newly retained, 7 both jointly, 15 with distractors reduced, and 7 with no new role retained -- so the gain is partly the intended structural recovery and partly a cleaner packet, NOT purely the claimed mechanism.
not_a_claim_about: packet budgets other than 6, which were not swept
S2b/S2c behaviour on surface forms, where they were inert and unmeasured
promotion of any selector into the default pipeline
the candidate-pool ceiling, which sits upstream and is unmeasured here
the reserved c2_cal_holdout, untouched
gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.not_earned_claim: S2c is the production selector for all V4 regimes.
gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.surface_partition_defect: S2b and S2c are INERT on descv4_surface: differs_from_s0=0.00 on every task. Question subjects there are truncated surface forms ('Ojos tension' vs canonical 'Ojos tension block'), so entity extraction yields no question entity on 100/100 tasks, no chains are enumerated, and packing falls back to pool order. Their surface figures are S0 replayed and are NOT measurements of those arms.
gate_c2s_selector_ladder_budget6.uncomfortable_result: On descv4_surface the rescoped relation-keyword control is the only arm with a significant gain: dQ=+0.1700, CI excluding zero under all three groupings, SGC 30.9%. It needs no entity extraction, so it still works where identity resolution fails. This does not rehabilitate it as a chain selector -- its BridgeRetention is 0.000 on descv4_id -- but it is not merely an artifact either.

gate_c3_final.claim: Gate C3 is closed. I3 identity-record retrieval is the qualified surface-normalization mechanism: 92% correct, 0% false resolution, 8% correct abstention on genuine conflicts, 92% S2cLiveRate. I0/I1/I2 are negative controls confirming the defect is identity-link resolution, not normalization or truncation. I4 is skipped due to insufficient opportunity.
gate_c3_final.earned_claim: Reading explicit surface-to-canonical mappings from runtime-visible identity records resolves the surface identity defect on a fresh sixth-vocabulary corpus with 92% accuracy and 0% false resolution.
not_a_claim_about: identity resolution being solved generally

sprint_a_retrieval_diagnosis.headline_finding: The retrieval 'availability collapse' is NOT a representation failure. On BOTH splits, 100% of missing required records are ranked by the frozen retrievers and merely fall below the candidate cutoff -- development 29/29, qualification 370/370. Zero unranked. CES reaches 100% at sufficient depth on both splits.
sprint_a_retrieval_diagnosis.method: Frozen receipts truncate bm25_ranked/bge_ranked/fusion_ranked at the candidate budget (50), so a required record at true rank 73 is indistinguishable from one at rank 2000 -- both merely absent. This re-runs the SAME frozen retrieval (query construction via run_query_stage, backends via get_cached_backend, fusion via retrieval_stage._rrf, corpus loading imported from run_gate_c4 rather than reimplemented) at full-corpus probe depth and records where required evidence actually ranks. Observation window widens; mechanism unchanged.
sprint_a_retrieval_diagnosis.plan_phases_this_affects: Phases 4-7 of the repair plan (structured query builder, role-aware retrieval passes, terminal-answer retrieval optimization, temporal query handling) were premised on required evidence being absent from retrieval. It is not absent -- it is ranked and truncated. Those phases may still be worth doing to raise evidence RANK (so it survives a tight budget), which is a different and more precisely stated objective than raising recall. Recommend re-scoping them around rank improvement plus the two separable repairs above, before building new retrieval mechanisms.
sprint_a_retrieval_diagnosis.produced_by: scripts/diagnose_c4_retrieval.py (CPU-only, no HRM, no mechanism change)

role_recall_at_frozen_budget.interpretation: Identity retrieval is solved on both splits (>=99%). The roles that starve under a tight budget are BRIDGE and TEMPORAL_CURRENT -- exactly the multi-hop roles, which rank lower and so are cut first. Consistent with budget starvation rather than representation failure, since all of them are ranked somewhere.

temporal_chain_reframed.corrected_reading: temporal_chain reaches 100% CES at sufficient depth and is 94.0% budget-recoverable. Its required records ARE retrieved and ranked, just deepest. Phase 7's temporal sub-experiment should therefore start by asking why temporal records rank low under a tight budget, not by adding temporal representation machinery.
temporal_chain_reframed.previous_reading: temporal_chain candidate CES 0.060 looked like a representation failure needing temporal embeddings / graph machinery.

the_generalization_artifact.interpretation: At equal ABSOLUTE budget the dev->qual gap is -13% to -32%. At equal corpus FRACTION the gap is +3.3% to -1.8%, i.e. indistinguishable. Retrieval's ranking quality generalizes essentially perfectly; the measured collapse is an artifact of holding a fixed absolute candidate budget (50) while the corpus grew 4.15x. This substantially revises the assumed repair: the retrieval lane is primarily a budget/pool-sizing question, not a query-reformulation or representation-learning question.

1_fusion_displacement_budget_neutral.finding: RRF discards required evidence that a single retriever already had INSIDE the budget: 88/370 qualification misses (23.8%), 7/29 development misses (24.1%). Of the qualification cases BM25 had 61 inside budget (median rank 37) and BGE had 27 (median rank 42).
1_fusion_displacement_budget_neutral.why_it_matters: This is recoverable WITHOUT enlarging the candidate pool, so it does not change what the selector must cope with. Cheapest available retrieval win and the one to test first.

2_budget_scaling_needs_a_protocol_versio.critical_unmeasured_interaction: Raising k is NOT established as a net win. A larger pool means more distractors for a selector already shown to drop 48% of AVAILABLE evidence (and to over-expand specifically on EXACT-identity tasks). Availability and final quality can move in opposite directions here. This interaction must be MEASURED on development before any budget change is frozen -- do not assume bigger k improves Q.
2_budget_scaling_needs_a_protocol_versio.finding: The remaining 76% of misses are genuinely below the cutoff and need a larger (or corpus-relative) budget.
2_budget_scaling_needs_a_protocol_versio.open_design_question: Whether the candidate budget should be corpus-relative rather than a fixed absolute constant. A fraction generalizes across these two corpora but will not scale to natural corpora where a fixed fraction of millions of documents is meaningless. Needs an explicit design decision, frozen in the new protocol, not a tuned constant.

sprint_b2_selector_repair.defect_repaired: EXACT AND BRIDGED. Keep-rate of available required evidence was EXACT_bridged 12.8% vs RESOLVED_bridged 95.0% on development -- multi-hop structure alone was not the problem, the failure was specific to EXACT+bridged (34 of 39 EXACT drops).
sprint_b2_selector_repair.frozen_mechanism: bridge_aware_anchor: protect the strongest candidate expressing the parsed target relation, anchored on the canonical subject OR an entity reachable by exactly ONE runtime-visible hop, when identity is EXACT; plus a connectivity constraint on the remaining slots. RESOLVED is left untouched. Protection consumes one slot of the SAME packet budget.
sprint_b2_selector_repair.leakage_discipline: Eligibility reads only record content, the relation parsed from the question, identity.canonical, and frozen fusion score/rank. record_kind is forbidden -- its values are generator answer-key labels. Enforced by a test that strips docstrings and asserts no executable statement touches record_kind/proof_edges/latent_bridge/answer_node/required_evidence_ids, plus a guard-the-guard test.
sprint_b2_selector_repair.next: Sprint B3 (budget scaling) or integration. Confirmation of S2 requires a FRESH untouched split; the qualification split is consumed and must not be used.
sprint_b2_selector_repair.rejected: S3 (temporal-current precedence) failed the increment requirement: Q 0.5125 vs S2 0.5250. Selection metrics alone could not distinguish them -- only downstream Q did, which is why it was kept as a required gate.

testing_policy: Tests assert structured state, never exact strings against narrative prose. Three separate failures came from matching capitalisation in text written separately from the assertion; the pattern was wrong, not merely careless. Prose is rendered from state, and state is what is tested.
